$comment: SEAM MANIFEST — which user-facing seams have a test that ENTERS the seam, not just the inner unit. A seam is COVERED only when the spec (a) exists, (b) contains seamEvent — the gesture/call proving it enters, and (c) contains negativeSpec — the no-op/refusal assertion. Statuses: COVERED (all three verified) · COVERED_NO_NEGATIVE (enters the seam, negative case MISSING — an honest admission) · OPEN (no seam-entering spec). The gate fails only on a FALSE claim, never on an honest admission. Evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-15-seam-coverage/SEAM-COVERAGE.md

seams.note: 8-9 of 12 specs are negative assertions. Added by e25d7cad after the shipped defect — the reference example.
Vertical drags stay on velocity editing instead of painting.
pointercancel abort and stale-pointerup cases are the ones that matter here.
No spec mentions resize or the right edge. Move is covered; resize is not.
Enters the seam and asserts the commit count, but has NO no-move / cancel case. This is the exact shape that hid the EQ bug. Honest admission, not a false claim.

ONLY the third spec enters the seam, and it does so with raw new PointerEvent(...) dispatch rather than fireEvent. The other two specs call the pure helper trimLeftEdge(doc, x) directly — a filename reading 'gesture' is not evidence of a gesture test.
Select tool keeps dragging — pointerdown does not split.

No pointerDown anywhere near a fade handle. clip-fade-bounds-invariant.test.ts is helper-only (no render, no dispatch). Note the intent layer gained a fade verb (P0-C) while the UI gesture is still uncovered.

Inherited from the shared Slider, not driven through the Mixer strip. Asserts the taper curve (log vs linear), not a no-op gesture, and uses one fixed clientX with no pointerMove — a move-sensitive defect would escape. Honest admission.
No spec clicks these buttons. mixer-batch.test.ts is command-level only.

LARGEST GAP. Zero pointerDown dispatches anywhere near the auto-canvas; ModPanel.test.tsx has fireEvent calls but no pointer event at all. The gesture most analogous to the EQ defect that shipped broken.

reaction-bridge.test.ts calls the function directly and guards the panel call site with a SOURCE-TEXT substring check — a text guard cannot prove behavior. tests/ui/IntentPanel.test.tsx clicks DO IT (traverses the seam) but never installs a ledger, so the call no-ops: traversal without assertion.
Compares the shipped manifest against the live grammar + hashes. This is the b7c1919c class of check, done right.
No spec asserts the loader's URL resolves to a file that exists. If MANIFEST_PATH drifts from the committed filename the artifact test stays green and the app 404s.
550 call sites across 37-41 spec files; the destructive-gate refusal specs are the negative case.
Dispatch to command is covered, but every ctx in the suite is a hand-rolled fake; dispatch -> REAL store -> undo depth is not asserted anywhere in the committed suite.

Driven through the real REC / STOP buttons, not the inner helper: a failed durable save must roll the already-playable resample back out of the bank (no ghost sample), offer no take and return the panel to idle. Verified by mutation — disabling the rollback in src/sample-library/bank-persist.ts turns exactly this spec red.

seams.negativeSpec: does not start a session for checkpoint save/list/diff
seams.note: Wave 1/A: the pre-session checkpoint is taken on the FIRST document-mutating call of a session only. Entered through the real headless MCP host (the same wrapper every transport uses); the negative specs pin that reads, runtime tools, dry-runs and checkpoint save/list/diff never start a session.

seams.negativeSpec: keeps the revert disabled while the session checkpoint is not durable
seams.note: Wave 1/A: the revert commits ONE undoable restoreSnapshot command from the panel, and closes the session. The negative spec pins that a non-durable checkpoint offers no revert at all (disabled, with the reason shown) instead of a button that cannot work.

seams.negativeSpec: aborts the owner's signal and settles as cancelled
seams.note: Wave 1/B: cancellation aborts the owner's signal and settles the job exactly once — the negative assertions pin that a cancelled job cannot be cancelled twice, cannot be revived by a late done(), and that the watchdog fails a lost owner instead of leaving it running.

seams.negativeSpec: stays quiet when the frozen buffer matches
seams.note: Wave 2/D: the strip is driven through the real component with a remembered signature — a mismatching signature shows the badge and RE-FREEZE, while a matching one AND an unknown one (no signature) both stay quiet, because an unprovable staleness must never be claimed.

seams.negativeSpec: keeps the file layout valid without an iXML chunk
seams.note: Wave 2/C: the manifest is written into a REAL encoded WAV and read back through the RIFF walker (hostile names/prompts, odd payload pad byte), and a file WITHOUT the chunk still has an exact RIFF size — the no-regression case for every existing exporter. The end-to-end step is pinned too: tests/ui/ExportPanel.test.tsx clicks EXPORT MASTER and parses the manifest out of the blob the panel hands to the save boundary.
